guide_lead: Every model works the weather out differently: some finely and for one region only, some coarsely for the whole world. Here is what each is good for – and how Windfenster chooses for your spot.
guide_whichLead: A start, not a law: where there are measurements, Windfenster marks with “Best here” which model actually hit best at that place lately.
guide_rNorth: North Sea and Baltic in Germany
guide_rAlps: Lakes in and north of the Alps
guide_autoText: Every hour a station compares what each model forecast with the wind it measured. From 14 days of data the page opens with the fine model that missed least on the first day and fills the ten days with the best global one. A point without a station takes the ranking of a station up to 5 km away; otherwise a fixed order applies.
guide_mixText: The mix averages all models every hour, weighted by how well each hit at this station. It opens the page only where it beat the best single model.
guide_classes: Superforecast is what the fine models are called (up to 2.2 km): hourly, but only for their region and mostly only two or three days. Forecast are the coarse ones: every 3 hours, but up to ten days and more.
guide_iconD2_area: Germany, the Benelux, Denmark, Switzerland, Austria and the edges of their neighbours.
guide_iconD2_good: Today and tomorrow on the North Sea and the Baltic, at inland lakes and north of the Alps. Fine enough to work out showers and thunderstorms itself instead of estimating them – what counts when a front or a squall line comes through.
guide_iconD2_watch: Reaches two days only; after that Windfenster fills in with the next model.
guide_iconCh1_good: The finest model here (1 km): valleys and lakes between mountains, where thermals and valley winds form on a small scale.
guide_iconCh1_watch: Reaches only into tomorrow (33 hours); Windfenster takes the rest of the day from the next fine model.
guide_iconCh2_good: The fine view of the next five days in the Alps, where the other fine models end after two or three days.
guide_iconCh2_watch: Coarser than ICON-CH1 (2 km) and updated less often.
guide_arome_area: France and its neighbours, with Corsica and the western Mediterranean.
guide_arome_good: French spots: the Mistral and Tramontane on the Mediterranean, the Atlantic and Brittany, wind squeezed between mountains. At 1.5 km one of the finest models.
guide_arome_watch: Reaches a little over two days.
guide_harmonie_area: Much of Europe, from Iceland to the Baltic.
guide_harmonie_good: Denmark, the North Sea and the Baltic, Scandinavia; at two and a half days it reaches further than ICON-D2 and AROME.
guide_harmonie_watch: It ends in Europe's south; others take over there.
guide_icon2i_area: Italy and around: Lake Garda, Sardinia, Sicily, the Adriatic.
guide_icon2i_good: Italian spots up to three days ahead, fine enough for Lake Garda's thermals.
guide_icon2i_watch: Only two runs a day: its forecast is often older than the others'.
guide_ecmwf_good: Planning several days ahead, anywhere in the world. In the weather services' comparisons it is mostly rated the most accurate global model.
guide_ecmwf_watch: At 25 km too coarse for thermals, wind funnelled between islands and the shape of a coast: at the spot often different from the forecast.
guide_ukmo_good: The second opinion next to ECMWF for the week, far from Europe too.
guide_ukmo_watch: Reaches seven days, so Windfenster never fills the ten days with it.
guide_iconEu_area: Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa.
guide_iconEu_good: The finest model where the fine ones end: around the Mediterranean, e.g. Rhodes, the Aegean with its Meltemi, southern Spain.
guide_iconEu_watch: Reaches five days; at 7 km still too coarse for small spots with thermals of their own.
guide_gfs_good: Sees furthest ahead (16 days) and is the base forecast of many wind apps – good for comparing.
guide_gfs_watch: Beyond a week only a trend; at 13 km too coarse for local effects.
